correctness.rationale: The unitary logarithmic transform reduces continuous Cesàro–Hardy to an upper Wiener–Hopf convolution with L1 kernel, and kernel multiplication gives its self-commutator as the negative square of the self-adjoint Hankel factor. The factor is nuclear by an absolutely trace-summable binomial rank-one expansion, and diagonal and double-integral beta evaluations prove both trace formulas. At integer orders Sylvester inertia of the independent monomials gives finite rank and exact signs. At noninteger orders the binomial coefficients have finitely many opposite signs and a uniform infinite tail sign: vanishing first moments yields an infinite definite subspace, and rescaled moment interpolants realize every opposing negative or positive direction; analyticity and polynomial density give injectivity. An executed standard-library script verifies 1102 exact rational finite assertions; finite checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: A self-commutator is an intrinsic Hilbert-space measure of nonnormality; its exact trace norm quantifies the continuous Cesàro–Hardy family rather than merely checking boundedness. The Hankel factor undergoes a nontrivial and complete finite/infinite rank and signed-index transition at each positive integer, with exact finite opposing indices on intervals; this has natural structural interpretation and leaves individual eigenvalue magnitudes open.
